incidents.victim: Kosovo credit card theft suspect (US consumer fraud victims)
incidents.vector: Suspect allegedly stole payment card and personal data from shopping websites using malware and sold it on criminal forums.
incidents.impact: A hard drive in the suspect's possession held 2.7 million stolen payment card numbers; he was extradited from Kosovo to face an eight-count indictment in Wisconsin.

incidents.vector: Audio/video transcription provider left customer data, including law enforcement body camera transcripts, exposed online.
incidents.impact: Sensitive law enforcement transcription data was publicly accessible before discovery.

incidents.vector: RansomwareHelp's CTO secretly paid ransomware groups (including LockBit) for decryptors while publicly claiming never to negotiate, then charged victims a large markup.
incidents.impact: An FBI sting led to a wire fraud indictment; one accounting-firm victim was charged $438,880 for a LockBit decryption obtained secretly for a fraction of that cost.

incidents.vector: Unattributed espionage group maintained access inside fragmented state administration networks for at least five years, evading detection due to lack of integrated monitoring.
incidents.impact: Tens of millions of government documents were stolen before the intrusion was discovered and the group evicted.

incidents.victim: EU politicians and law enforcement officials
incidents.vector: Pro-Kremlin hacktivist group NoName057(16) published personal information obtained on high-profile individuals.
incidents.impact: 18 EU officials were doxxed, including Italy's foreign minister, Europol's cybercrime chief, and journalists covering Russian hacking.

incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote-access service to connect to customer devices and install backdoors.
incidents.impact: Travel routers and IP KVM devices were backdoored; GL.iNet blocked the attack path and released firmware fixes, though infected devices may need a factory reset.

incidents.victim: Financial services, healthcare, and legal organizations (US, UK, Australia)
incidents.vector: Com-affiliated actors (Bling Libra/ShinyHunters and related clusters) use vishing calls impersonating IT support to steal credentials and MFA approvals via adversary-in-the-middle proxies, then exfiltrate Microsoft 365/OneDrive/SharePoint data.
incidents.impact: Victims have had tens of millions of CRM and patient records stolen, with attackers broadcasting extortion demands via Teams/email and directing victims to Tor negotiation sites.

incidents.vector: Company says an attacker used AI tools to breach its systems rapidly.
incidents.impact: 1984 Hosting, Iceland's largest web host, shut down services to protect customer data, taking tens of thousands of customer sites offline.

incidents.vector: Attacker used authentic credentials leaked by a third party to access the Rackspace Spot cloud marketplace.
incidents.impact: Kubernetes secrets were stolen from customer accounts, and intruders deployed their own pods in affected environments.

incidents.victim: Unibet and other FDJ United platforms
incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against FDJ United's online betting infrastructure.
incidents.impact: FDJ United took down sports-betting platform Unibet and several online casinos; no details on attack nature were provided.

incidents.vector: Multiple cyberattacks hit the agency, prompting suspension of all services as a precaution.
incidents.impact: No evidence of data theft found; IMT is the fourth Portuguese government body targeted in recent weeks.

incidents.victim: Federal Bureau of Investigation (National Crime Information Center)
incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into the FBI's NCIC database of warrants, fugitives, and investigation records shared across law enforcement.
incidents.impact: Breach under investigation; the FBI's second major incident this year after the ShinyHunters breach of its HR portal in September, potentially exposing investigative files.

incidents.victim: Mr. Cooper (Nationstar Mortgage) customers; Rocket Mortgage
incidents.vector: Threat actors impersonated Mr. Cooper employees on calls to trick the IT help desk into issuing temporary passwords, bypassing MFA.
incidents.impact: Large amounts of private customer data were stolen in the November 2023 breach; NY DFS fined Rocket Mortgage (which later acquired Mr. Cooper) $6.75 million combined for MFA and reporting failures.

incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a bug in the Entra Connect Health API, introduced by a July update, to scrape tenant configuration data.
incidents.impact: Administrator emails and tenant configuration data were collected before Microsoft deployed a fix.

incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a vulnerability in older 'Classic' tiers of Azure API Management to access tokens and credentials stored in the platform.
incidents.impact: Both energy firms detected attacks targeting credentials; Equinor's internal services were disrupted (production unaffected), and Norwegian authorities warned the flaw affects organizations across sectors and countries.

incidents.vector: Newly identified group 'SilentAir' hacks telco infrastructure and plants backdoors exploiting SS7 and Diameter signaling protocols.
incidents.impact: The group has collected device data, tracked subscriber locations, and intercepted calls/SMS of selected targets since early 2025.

incidents.victim: ~700 French retail stores, butchers, food factories, and a slaughterhouse
incidents.vector: IRGC's Shahid Kaveh military cyber unit hacked commercial refrigeration systems, causing freezer failures.
incidents.impact: The October attack caused tens of millions of euros in losses across roughly 700 sites; French officials attributed it to Iran on Nov. 17.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations (media, technology, financial services brands using Optimizely)
incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a flaw in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer accounts, served from Optimizely's legitimate CDN under its own certificate.
incidents.impact: For about 16 hours, 178+ sites served code that swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed payment card data, and attempted to deliver mobile exploit kits; Optimizely patched the flaw within a day.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against the fundraising platform.
incidents.impact: DonorPerfect took systems offline and has not clarified whether customer or donor data was stolen while gradually restoring service.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against the specialty retailer.
incidents.impact: The company says it has recovered its systems following the attack.

incidents.vector: USDA's security team discovered a breach affecting applications used to issue payments to American farmers.
incidents.impact: Payment applications have been offline over a week while IT staff reset passwords across all databases.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupted an IT platform Nissan repair shops use to diagnose vehicles.
incidents.impact: Repair shops have been unable to diagnose cars, ship firmware fixes, or replace key fobs since Nov. 13.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a ministry website operated by an external service provider.
incidents.impact: Names and official contact details of ministry staff in Vienna and abroad were accessed; the ministry says the breach was contained with no public data compromised.

incidents.vector: Files on the agency's file-sharing service were left exposed online due to a configuration issue.
incidents.impact: Government files were publicly accessible for three and a half months (Jul. 30–Nov. 12) before discovery.

incidents.vector: A shared third-party provider was breached, exposing limited data belonging to customers of all three financial firms.
incidents.impact: Breaches claimed by extortion group 'n0n'; companies describe the exposed data as limited in scope.

incidents.vector: Attacker used a cloud access key Barracuda issued to a third-party AI provider and forgot to revoke, then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access.
incidents.impact: Attacker accessed Barracuda's cloud environment for nearly two days before being discovered and removed.

incidents.vector: Attacker compromised a DevOps engineer's laptop, reached a service container, and submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
incidents.impact: More than $6 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen; authorities have frozen, seized, or returned over $2.9 billion, including a $1.1 billion forfeiture action announced Nov. 23.

incidents.victim: Universities across East Asia (outside mainland China)
incidents.vector: A China-linked actor used autonomous Cairn AI agents, discovering a zero-day in an exposed medical imaging application and gaining root access to a server in about 11 minutes.
incidents.impact: The roughly 48-hour campaign also included unsuccessful attempts against a Redis instance and over 30,000 SSH credential combinations; Amazon Threat Intelligence assesses the agents operated largely without human direction.

incidents.victim: 19 organizations across semiconductor manufacturing, U.S. defense policy, and civil society
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers ran 25 autonomous operations using the open-source Cairn AI pentesting framework paired with GLM and DeepSeek models, given only a target and goal.
incidents.impact: Ten organizations were compromised, including exposure of over one million records at a teachers' union, theft of valid credentials, and creation of persistent admin accounts in a semiconductor company's production system.
